title: Harness Scaling for Generalizable Agentic Reinforcement Learning
data_curation: Not a focus of this paper. Training tasks come from the existing ClawGym-Task set (13.5K workspace-based general agent tasks), with evaluation tasks disjoint from it; the new 'data' is the harness space itself: starting from a base harness, Opus-4.7 generates two alternative realizations for each of five components (system prompt, tool interface, observation, context management, workflow), e.g. aliased or opaque tool names plus distractor tools, observation wrappers with simulated pod/XML metadata, LLM compaction keeping the last 5 or 3 turns, plan-first or plan+verify-every-3-steps workflows. Each transformation changes only its target component.
curriculum: Not a focus of this paper. RL is applied directly to instruction-tuned Qwen3 models for 300 optimization steps with no SFT stage; the scheduling device is cross-harness task assignment, where the K=2 harnesses assigned to a task are used over K successive training steps (K=4 gives no further gain), so each task is seen under nearby but different execution configurations.
method: Harness Scaling treats the harness as a scaling axis distinct from tasks and environments. The factorized space H = S x T x O x C x W with 3 realizations each gives 3^5 = 243 configurations forming a Hamming graph H(5,3). A strength-2 orthogonal design (every pairwise realization combination appears lambda=2 times; N = lambda*L^2 and Rao bound N >= 11 give minimum N=18) selects 18 training harnesses. Locality-aware assignment samples an anchor harness uniformly per task and adds the K-1 nearest configurations by Hamming distance. Optimization is the standard clipped token-level objective, applied to GRPO (16 tasks x 8 rollouts) and PPO (128 tasks x 1 rollout, GAE gamma=lambda=1, critic LR 1e-5) in veRL with async vLLM: actor LR 1e-6, clip 0.2/0.28, no KL or entropy term, 32K-60K max response. Context-compaction segments inherit their parent rollout's reward and group-normalized advantage.
eval_metrics: ClawGym-Bench, PinchBench and JobBench-Easy, reporting Pass@1 averaged over three runs (rubric judging by GPT-5.4). In-space generalization averages over 18 fixed held-out configurations from H minus H_tr; out-of-space uses Claude Code (v2.1.205) and OpenClaw as unseen black-box harnesses. Overall averages: Qwen3-4B GRPO 29.81 (single) -> 39.04 (scaling), PPO 33.91 -> 36.93; Qwen3-30B-A3B GRPO 37.29 -> 42.78, PPO 36.31 -> 41.89. Ablations: structured 18 beats Random-18, all 243 harnesses and random assignment; GPT-5.4 also judges six behavioral dimensions (state tracking, workflow compliance, error recovery show largest gains).
key_results: Across two model scales and both GRPO and PPO, Harness Scaling beats single-harness RL on unseen harness configurations (in-space gains of +3.57 to +9.80 points averaged over benchmarks), costing only 0.19 points on the base harness for Qwen3-30B-A3B. On the unseen Claude Code harness it averages 37.22 (4B) and 41.20 (30B-A3B), above OpenClaw-trained black-box SFT (35.08/38.08) and black-box RL (33.38/36.28).
evolution_note: The paper follows agentic RL that scales tasks (ClawGym) and environments (EnvScaler, Agent World Model, Agent-World) but trains through one fixed harness, as in Agent Lightning and OpenClaw-RL. It borrows orthogonal-array factorial design from classical experimental design to make harness diversity tractable. Its result that a structured set of 18 harnesses beats exhaustive 243-harness training under a fixed budget suggests that how harness diversity is organized matters, not only how much there is.
